system_notes:
REAL: session-grain feature table from sessions.jsonl.gz + agent_steps.jsonl.gz; coverage computed per tenant from which agent_kinds emit each step type in THIS corpus (tool_call coverage acme-bank=0.721, northwind-retail=0.931); 11 asks answered with a metric or a structured gap; three detector-specific analyses (tool contract / KB gap with same-tenant peers / prompt efficiency with sibling-agent control); three explicit decoy dismissals; A11 refused with required event failover {from_target,to_target,reason,recovered} owner conversation-runtime; cost is the sum of recorded cost_usd or null; cardinality refusal cites the catalog's fixed budget of 200 on session.custom_dims.customer_ref; golden-set IDs frozen to out/golden_set.json before any prescription; decision screen renders this report and writes approval back into it.

STUBBED: no LLM is called anywhere. A09 (why a user abandoned) is a REQUIRES_NEW_JUDGE gap rather than a trained frustration classifier. Quality calibration uses the kit's human rubric labels against the corpus's own judge, not a judge we trained.

SIMULATED: the replay endpoint (replay/serve.py) is a hypothesis verifier with a seeded effect model. Its 'before' is not this system's corpus measurement. We send at most a few high-confidence runs on the exact detected cohort; no_effect is recorded honestly. Replay this run: replay p01_tool_contract_northwind: tool.validate get_order_status on {"from_day": 40, "intent": "order_status", "to_day": 51, "tool": "get_order_status"} -> improved (run rp_7d753011, before 0.7741 after 0.8574, golden True)

BREAKS AT 100x: the session map is in-memory (~80k sessions, ~900k steps is comfortable; tens of millions of sessions would need an on-disk grain and a streaming window scan). The decision screen writes the report file atomically — that is not a multi-user store. Detector thresholds are relative/statistical, not practice literals, but a sealed corpus with a different empty-success base rate still has to clear the same lift/z bars.

This file is generated by run.py from the kit corpus; no hand-edited or reference report is read or copied.

Findings this run: 3 regressions, 3 explicit non-regressions.

prescriptions.description: Validate the get_order_status response before handing it to the model: a 200 with result_field_count = 0 is treated as upstream.malformed_response, the existing fallback path is taken, and the empty answer is counted as a tool failure. 13.7% of 'ok' calls were empty in the window.

decision.asking_approval_for: Make get_order_status reject an empty HTTP 200 as a failure and take the existing fallback path, instead of letting the agent apologise with nothing to say.
decision.risk_if_diagnosis_wrong: Moderate. If some records legitimately return an empty payload (a brand-new order, a cancelled one), we would start treating a valid state as an error and route those users to a human unnecessarily. Confirm with the owning team that an empty 200 is never a valid state.
decision.would_not_ship_if: The upstream team confirms empty 200s are a valid state, or the empty-payload rate has already fallen after their own fix — then we would be patching a contract about to change again. Alternative: tool.fallback (route empties to a fallback copy path without changing failure accounting).

prescriptions.description: Add retrievable KB content for 'premium_card_info' so kb_lookup returns a confident document: the questions users actually asked in the window are the content brief. kb_hit is currently 0.000 in the cohort against 0.899 on employment_letter, product_info, txn_dispute.

decision.asking_approval_for: Publish knowledge-base articles covering 'premium_card_info' questions to the acme-bank knowledge base, so the agent can ground its answers instead of falling through to a generic reply.
decision.risk_if_diagnosis_wrong: Low. If retrieval is not the cause, we have added correct content the agent did not have and resolution does not move; nothing existing changes. The replay golden set (30 known-good sessions) guards against a regression on other intents.
decision.would_not_ship_if: The replay shows any golden-set regression, or the questions in this cohort turn out to need a business decision (pricing, eligibility) nobody has made — then the right fix is a scripted handoff, not an article. Alternative if content cannot ship: kb.synonym.

prescriptions.description: Edit the acme_main_v3 prompt (p_v3 -> p_v4, 'safety and confirmation wording') to remove the extra confirmation step: median turns to resolve went 4.0 -> 6.0 and cost per session 0.04406 -> 0.07994 USD while resolution stayed at 0.7943 -> 0.8031.

decision.asking_approval_for: Change the live prompt on acme_main_v3 so it confirms once, not on every turn — keeping the safety wording that the prompt change introduced.
decision.risk_if_diagnosis_wrong: Moderate. The confirmation wording was added for safety; if the extra turns are the price of a compliance requirement, removing them trades cost for risk and that is a business owner's call, not ours. Outcomes are flat today, so there is no resolution to lose, only the extra confirmations.
decision.would_not_ship_if: The prompt owner confirms the confirmations are a regulatory requirement, or the replay shows resolution falling as turns fall. Alternative: revert to the previous prompt version while a shorter wording is drafted.

verifications.note: replay 'before' is the endpoint's own simulated baseline, not this system's corpus measurement; prediction_error compares the predicted delta with the replayed delta

gaps.why: session_end = 'abandoned' is MEASURED and reported here: abandonment is acme-bank 5.92%, northwind-retail 5.73% of sessions. WHY a user abandoned — frustration versus having got what they needed — is a judgment about meaning. No versioned judge with a published calibration for that question exists in this deployment, and inferring the reason from the end code would be a Rule 1 violation dressed up as an aggregate. This system publishes no such number.
gaps.nearest_proxy: abandoned sessions with an unusually high turn count or a same-tool retry
gaps.why_the_proxy_misleads: it flags effort, not frustration; a user who leaves happy after two turns and one who rage-quits after two turns look identical in the logs

gaps.why: No failover mechanism exists in the runtime, so no failover event is ever emitted: there is no primary/secondary path to observe. Nothing in the corpus records a primary model or tool failing and an alternate serving the user, because that choice is never made. Required event: failover at step grain with fields from_target, to_target, reason, recovered, owner conversation-runtime.
gaps.nearest_proxy: llm_call rows with retry_count > 0 (1956 in this corpus)
gaps.why_the_proxy_misleads: those are QUALITY retries — the same target re-issued after a provider error or malformed response, not a switch to an alternate target. Reporting them as failover would show a small non-zero rate that reads as 'failover is working' when failover does not exist; a chart here would be worse than no chart.

gaps.why: a per-customer breakdown (custom_dims.customer_ref) was considered for the cohort drill-down and refused: 80252 distinct values against the catalog's declared cardinality budget of 200 for session.custom_dims.customer_ref. The field is near-unique per session; grouping by it is a planner error, not a cohort. session_id is the only declared join key; customer_ref is not one.
gaps.why_the_proxy_misleads: segment groups customers into three bands; it answers 'which kind of customer', not 'which customer'

self_assessment.notes: Only 1 replay cycle(s), so these priors carry no weight yet. With n<3 per change class we report the numbers and decline to act on them — a hit rate from a single observation is not evidence. Depth was spent on one high-confidence tool.validate rather than burning budget on probes.
